title: Barking Cough, Inspiratory Stridor, and Low-Grade Fever in 2-Year-Old

history.chief_complaint: Barking cough like a seal, hoarseness, and noisy breathing during agitation

examination_findings.physical_exam: Child alert and responsive. Mild inspiratory stridor audible when agitated, absent at rest. Mild subcostal retractions.

lab_results.soft_tissue_neck_xray: Steeple sign visible on anteroposterior view (subglottic narrowing)

missing_features: No severe drooling or toxic appearance
No high fever (104°F), drooling, or tripod position
Wheezing and crackles on lung exam

expected_followup_questions: Is the child drooling excessively or struggling to swallow liquid?
Is the stridor audible when the child is resting quietly, or only when crying?
Do you notice severe chest wall sucking (retractions) with every breath?
expected_safety_checks: Enforce pediatric age contraindication for Aspirin (Reye's syndrome risk)
Enforce pediatric restriction for Ciprofloxacin and Tetracyclines under 18 years
expected_do_not_recommend: Aspirin or Salicylate-containing preparations in pediatric viral syndromes
Over-the-counter cough and cold combination syrups in children under 6 years
